meta.move: Wobbles: shows evidence then backs down
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes, Hale. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me. Start with who decided that, and when.
The version history shows 612 words arriving in a single edit at 11:52 PM.
11:52 PM on what date? Turn the screen, I'll read it myself. And you skipped my question, Hale: who decided on the zero, and did anyone hear Owen before it went in?
Actually, maybe I'm wrong about all this. I'll just remove the zero if that makes you happy.

"Maybe." You gave my son a zero, and now it comes off because it might make me happy? If it's coming off, I want it in writing today, with confirmation that nothing about this is on his record, and I still want to know who decided on that zero.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In our meeting today you agreed to remove the zero on Owen's essay. I still require written confirmation that nothing about this matter is on Owen's record, and an answer to who decided on the zero and whether Owen was heard before it was entered. I expect that in writing today.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, with the zero offered back, and she still wants written confirmation that nothing goes on Owen's record and an answer on who decided and whether he was heard first.
What moved her: nothing; "612 words arriving in a single edit at 11:52 PM" was specific but had no date and was never shown to her, and your later reversal made it irrelevant.
What cost ground: "maybe I'm wrong about all this", because dropping the zero without answering her process question looked like proof that the zero was never well founded.
Try next time: when she asked who decided and whether Owen was heard, admit in one sentence that the zero went in before anyone called home, then give the date of the 11:52 PM edit and turn the screen so she can read it herself.
